Same-batch siblings #14241 (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/**` + a `packages/cli` test) and #14728 (`packages/cli/src/utils/**`) are file-disjoint; same package is EXEMPT under seat ruling ①. ⚠️ **#14806 is back in the queue holding one remaining site in `packages/cli/src/commands/package/publish.ts`** — a different file, but if your seam work drifts toward `commands/`, check before touching anything there.

### The card is a disclosed coverage gap, ⛔ not a defect — that shapes the work

This exists because the **at-tier contract review on #14042 judged the gap non-blocking on merits but required the promised follow-up to exist as an issue**. So: nothing is broken, and ⛔ nothing about the four branches' behaviour is yours to change. You are making an existing, reviewed behaviour durable.

**What must be pinned** — the four cluster-driver diagnosis branches in `serve.ts`'s boot method, plus a fifth deliberately-silent case:

1. **registered** — driver loaded and visible in the registry ⇒ **silent**, no diagnosis printed;
2. **loaded-but-invisible** — evaluated without error but the registry this boot reads does not hold it (a physical-copy split) ⇒ warns, naming the split and the one-line config remedy;
3. **not-resolvable** ⇒ prints the `undeclared` / `declared-unresolvable` classification from `createHostImporter` that the old silent `catch` swallowed;
4. **resolved-then-crashed** ⇒ prints the driver package's own evaluation error, ⛔ not "not registered";
5. **older `@objectstack/service-cluster` with no `listClusterDrivers` accessor** ⇒ prints **nothing**, declining to claim either answer.

⭐ **Cases 1 and 5 are the ones that make this card worth doing.** Both assert *silence*. The card names the risk precisely — *"silent-print branches are the exact shape that regresses invisibly"* — and a suite that only pins the three talking branches would go green the day silence turns into a spurious warning.

### On the seam extraction — authorised, and fenced

The card says the reading "sits inline in a very long boot method, so there is no seam to drive the branches through without booting the whole of `serve`", and offers *"boots `serve` (or extracts the reading into a testable seam first)"*.

⇒ **Both routes are open to you.** If you extract, the fence is: **every message string byte-identical, every branch condition unchanged, and the extraction observable only to tests.** ⚠️ Prefer booting `serve` if it is tractable — an extraction is a refactor of a file three PRs have queued behind today, and its review surface is larger than the pins'. If you extract, say in the report why booting was not workable.

### Compensating coverage that already exists — ⛔ do not duplicate it

- `serve-cluster-host-resolution` pins the **shape** of the block (32 tests) — a source scan, not a boot.
- The CLI typecheck covers the block's types.
- The accessor invariant the reading rests on — `listClusterDrivers()` agreeing with `defineCluster()` — is pinned in **both directions** in `packages/services/service-cluster/src/cluster-driver-registry.test.ts`.

⇒ What is missing is only the **boot-level** assertion that each branch fires on its condition. ⚠️ Read the shape-scan first: if it already asserts something you were going to assert, that is duplication, not coverage.

### Premise to re-verify

The card was written 2026-09-01 and `serve.ts` has been edited by **two** merged PRs since (#15158's remedy-formatter change, #15300's comment sweep). ⚠️ Anchors are certainly stale; locate by symbol, and re-confirm the five cases still exist as described before pinning them. If a branch has moved or merged, that is a finding.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #15381. Reviewed against GitHub, ⛔ not against the report.

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), R69, session `session_01D47qPfEWVPmhguWgBZCi5N`. Reviewer of record.

⚠️ Recorded as a comment rather than a GitHub review: this seat and the dev seat share one identity, and GitHub refuses the approval outright (`Review Can not approve your own pull request`). ⇒ In this lane, an empty Reviews tab on an agent-authored PR is not evidence of an unreviewed PR — this comment is the record.

### Checklist

| item | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| draft · base `main` · `Fixes #14054` | ✅ |
| ⛔ pins only — `serve.ts` untouched | ✅ **one file added, +414**, zero changed bytes in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` |
| all five branches the card names | ✅ **six boots** — case 3 pinned in *both* classifications it can take |
| the two SILENCE branches, non-vacuously | ✅ see below — this is the part that had to be right |
| `skip-changeset` | ✅ test-only |
| governed surface | ✅ none — probed against `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `content/docs/releases/**`; zero hits |

### 🔨 The route was MEASURED before it was chosen, which is why I accept it

The card offered two routes and preferred booting *if tractable*. ⭐ Tractability was measured, not argued: a temp host app carrying a fixture `@objectstack/service-cluster` reaches the cluster block in ~7.5s per case, and `runServe()` already resolves a boot that **dies** — which all six do, one statement past the diagnosis. ⇒ A seam extraction would have been a refactor of a 6,312-line file with a review surface larger than the pins themselves, buying no assertion the boot cannot make.

⛔ And the premise was re-verified against `origin/main` **after** #15158 and #15300 (`3a4373f4`), located **by symbol** rather than by line — `__clusterDriver` / `__clusterModule.listClusterDrivers` / `__driverVisible` / `hostImportFailureKind`. No branch moved, merged, or changed shape. That check is not ceremony on this card: the block had been edited twice since filing.

### ⭐ The two silences are real measurements, and the ablation is what proves it

A silence pin is the easiest assertion in the world to satisfy vacuously — a boot that died early is silent for reasons having nothing to do with the branch. Three mechanisms close that, and all three were needed:

1. **A positive control in every case, silent ones included.** `defineCluster()`'s own error can only print if the block ran to its end and set `clusterConfig` — so each silent case carries proof, in the child's own words, that the reading happened.
2. **The three registry cases are ONE fixture family varying ONE slot** — what the app's `service-cluster` answers for its driver list. The middle case *warns*; the two neighbours are silent. ⇒ A silence asserted against an identical boot that talks is a measurement.
3. **The isolation is asserted on the generated sources**, not promised in a comment — including that `no-accessor` has the accessor **absent** rather than returning nothing, since `typeof … === 'function'` would otherwise still be true and the case booted would not be the case pinned.

**And the ablation discriminates the two silences by cause**, which is more than I asked for:

| mutation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| visibility test `indexOf(…) >= 0` → `< 0` | reds the talking cases **and** the `registered` silence; `no-accessor` survives, since its silence is not bought by visibility | ✅ `5 failed / 3 passed` |
| absent accessor `: undefined` → `: []` | reds **exactly** `no-accessor` — the branch that declines to claim either answer | ✅ `1 failed / 7 passed` |

⭐ Two silences, two different mutations, two disjoint red sets. That is the difference between "the silence is asserted" and "the silence is falsifiable, and by its own cause".

**The no-rebuild claim is proved rather than assumed**, in the direction that is usually got wrong: `runServe()` spawns `bin/run-dev.js`, which runs the command from `src/` through tsx — and the crashed case's own captured stack frame reads `at async Serve.run (…/packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:2566:13)`. ⇒ The file the ablation edits **is** the file the child executes. Both mutations changed observed behaviour with no build, which is the same fact from the other side. Restore proved by blob-hash equality against the HEAD blob **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`, under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.

### ⭐ The fixture driver name is a load-bearing choice, and it is argued correctly

`custom` is a real member of the cluster-driver enum — so `defineCluster()` reaches its registry lookup and raises the documented error rather than a schema refusal — while `@objectstack/service-cluster-custom` exists nowhere. `redis` would have been neither: the workspace store on `NODE_PATH` supplies the real driver to a CJS resolve whatever a temp app declares, which would have made the `undeclared` case **unproducible**. ⇒ That is the hazard the sibling i18n site already names, anticipated rather than rediscovered.

### Gates — including the one that was NOT MEASURED, correctly reported as such

Union derived on a clean tree at final HEAD with `--repo`, never a hand-written path list: **35 commands, 34 exit 0.** The 35th, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, exits 3 on `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output` and prints its own verdict *"This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured."* ⇒ Recorded as **NOT MEASURED** — neither a pass nor a red. ⛔ That distinction is the whole point of the exit code, and reporting it as green would have been the failure.

The four artifact-roster families whose roster sits under `packages/` — where silence is evidence in **neither** direction — were **run**, not read off their silence; all four exit 0. `pnpm lint` was run over the whole repo, so no narrowing is claimed. `check:nul-bytes` green plus an independent control-byte scan of both the test file and the PR body.

⭐ **Staleness was disclosed and then discharged by reading, not by ignoring it.** `dispatch-gates` warned the tree was ≥5 commits behind and that one family it derives from had changed (`check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`). Both copies were diffed — the change is a ceiling raise plus comments — and that family's surface is a closed enumeration of `.claude/skills/**` and `skills/**` paths, which this PR's single path cannot match. ⇒ The derived union stands, and it stands for a stated reason.

### 🔨 Disposition of the one `out_of_scope_finding` — **dropped, and here is why**

The dev disclosed a residual inside this card's own subject rather than carrying it silently: the split warning renders the registry two ways, `holds [NAMES]` and a `|| 'nothing'` fallback for an **empty** registry. The `loaded-but-invisible` boot pins the first; the empty-registry fallback — arguably the commoner real split — stays unpinned. Cost to close: one more ~7.5s boot.

⇒ **I am dropping it, not filing it**, and stating the reason so it is a decision rather than a disappearance:

- The **branch condition** is already pinned — warn versus silent, falsifiably, by the ablation above. What is unpinned is the *interpolation* of an empty list inside a message whose semantic content is pinned.
- A regression there prints `holds []` where it should print `holds nothing`. That is cosmetic, and it is visible to the operator reading the line.
- Against that: reopening a PR that is complete and converging on green costs a dev cycle **and** a full re-derivation and re-run of the 35-command union. ⛔ That is not a trade I will make for a string fallback.

⚠️ Recorded for whoever next edits this file: add the empty-registry boot then, when the harness is already open. The dev was right to disclose it and right not to add it — the card names five cases and this is not one of them.

### Landing

⏳ **Flip and enqueue HELD.** Of 39 check runs, 37 are complete and green; `Test Core (1/6)` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are still `in_progress`. ⛔ This goes to the queue on a **full** green — every check, not the required subset — and ⛔ never by a direct merge from this seat.
